arjun: ran a 30m side-by-side comparing our replay harness vs synthetic load on the 8xA100 pool. quick hit: replay gives lower tail in non-stream mode but streaming replay shows higher p50 variance. synth is smoother but ~15% lower peak throughput. attaching a few numbers below.

maria: can you drop the exact commands and the batching/kv config you used? want to reproduce. :eyes:

arjun: sure — main invocations: 
```
./run_replay.py --trace path/to/trace.json --pool 8A100 --streaming=true --chunk-size=128 --batch-policy=heuristic_v3 
./run_synth.py --rps 800 --seq-dist long --streaming=false --batch-policy=heuristic_v3
```
kv config (short): `kv.prefetch=0.2`, `kv.max_entries=1_000_000`, `kv.warm_threshold=0.75`

tj: note on KV: cold replays spike p99 until KV hit-rate ~80%. saw p99 jump from 180ms -> 450ms for first ~3 minutes if we don't prewarm. profiling points to `kv_read_loop` contending on rwlock and doing async io bursts. median kv read ~1.7ms, but tail reads >10ms during cold start. prewarm top-10% prefixes and p99 stabilizes.

alan: fyi I noticed a regression after kernel-selector v2 landed — streaming tests with chunk-size=128 had p95 +40ms vs prior selector. hypothesis: selector picks the new fp16 small-batch matmul kernel which is faster at large batches but worse at tiny batch sizes, so streaming (many small micro-batches) pays a penalty. can we force the legacy kernel for a quick A/B?

maria: let's avoid cross-run infra noise — I propose interleaved side-by-side on the same cluster: run both clients concurrently but tag requests so routing picks the same model instance. that isolates host-level noise. also lock the client readloop to deterministic backoff to avoid client jitter. config snippet: 
```
client.readloop:{
  max_inflight:4,
  backoff_ms:20,
  chunk_size:128,
  jitter_seed:42
}
```

arjun: good call on deterministic readloop. I'll run: 1) replay streaming with prewarm + selector=v2, 2) replay streaming with prewarm + selector=legacy, 3) synth streaming same configs. will collect flamegraphs and kernel call counts. estimate ~2h.

tj: small operational note — client-side backpressure: when chunk size <64 we see many tiny write syscalls and the client ack loop becomes the limiter (increased latency variance). bumping chunk to 128 reduced syscall rate by ~3x and improved throughput by ~8% in streaming mode. worth adding to benchmarking checklist.

alan: after forced-legacy run, if perf improves we need to tweak selector heuristics (batch size threshold + model_seq_len cutoff). also add unit that records chosen kernel id per request to trace for future analysis.

maria: agreed. add a test case that replays a 30m production trace but with prewarm toggled and kernel forced, then compute delta matrix: {mode x prewarm x selector} -> p50/p95/p99/throughput/kv-hit. we can store as single csv for plotting.

arjun: starting runs now. will post a short summary + raw numbers + links to flamegraphs when done. :thumbsup:
